entry.title: ‘What To The Slave Is The Fourth Of July?’: Descendants Read Frederick Douglass' Speech
entry.quote: In the summer of 2020, the U.S. commemorated Independence Day amid nationwide protests for racial justice and systemic reforms in the wake of George Floyd’s death. That June, we asked five young descendants of Frederick Douglass to read and respond to excerpts of his famous speech, “What to the Slave is the Fourth of July?”. It's a powerful, historical text that reminds us of the ongoing work of liberation.

entry.title: The Boeing 747 Begins Its Final Descent
entry.quote: The jet was perhaps the pinnacle of American engineering excellence. Its retirement signals an end to an era of American culture—and ambition.

entry.title: My family has been here since 1621. That is not what makes me American: Philip Bump
entry.quote: Let's look at ancestry, immigration, Revolutionary War service and July 4 as the United States marks its 250th birthday.

entry.title: How a coastline 100 million years ago influences modern election results in Alabama
entry.quote: Here I’ve gathered 6 maps of the US state of Alabama. Together, these maps tell a story that links a coastline from the time of the dinosaurs, to modern political demographics, via one of the darkest periods of American history.
